CIGRE Calgary 2026 · SC C1 · Paper 10502

Integration of Large Loads to the Ontario Power System

Mohamed Shamseldein · Fang Gao · Mahmoud Bayoumi
Independent Electricity System Operator (IESO), Canada

CIGRE Energy Forum · Calgary, Alberta · September 21–24, 2026

Read / download PDFOfficial CIGRE proceedings

Author-provided copy · PDF · 10 pages. Please cite the CIGRE Calgary 2026 proceedings. The official proceedings are available through eCIGRE.

Summary

Large computational loads (LCLs) connect in large blocks and combine uninterruptible-power-supply switchover, backup-generation transfer, fast active-power ramps, and the potential for periodic oscillation and load fluctuation. These behaviours can appear to the power system as abrupt load rejection, uncontrolled load loss or adverse control interaction. Ontario's existing Market Rules, written for conventional load, do not quantify these behaviours. This paper explains how the IESO developed new and enhanced technical reliability requirements for LCLs. A common structure links each requirement to the electrical behaviour, reliability risk and Market-Rule gap that motivated it, then identifies the assessment method, compliance evidence and facility obligation. The requirements address connection arrangement, voltage and frequency ride-through, ramping, fluctuation and oscillation, monitoring and validated models. The System Impact Assessment is extended with dynamic and electromagnetic-transient studies and staged as project data mature. Public engagement clarified the applicable transmission and distribution connection boundaries, introduced distinct voltage ride-through profiles for those interfaces, and refined the evidence needed from design through commissioning. The resulting framework combines system-wide reliability limits with project-specific assessment and mitigation.

Citation

M. Shamseldein, F. Gao and M. Bayoumi, “Integration of Large Loads to the Ontario Power System,” CIGRE Calgary 2026 Colloquium, SC C1, paper 10502, pp. 1–10, 2026.
